tws-sony-wf-1000xm6.tagline: Widest stereo imaging, most comfortable ANC, king of bean-shaped TWS
tws-sony-wf-1000xm6.review: Oh, the timbre in the mids. Crank it up and it's insanely natural: dynamic-driver timbre that's very studio-monitor-like. Front-to-back depth and top-to-bottom dimension feel even bigger. Not as bright as the Buds 3 Pro and MTW4, though. The ANC blocks people talking even better, yet it's still comfortable; 8 ANC mics in a TWS is crazy. The mic improved too. Only the price is heavy. The bean-shaped TWS to beat, hands down. (Full review on his YouTube.)

tws-samsung-galaxy-buds4-pro.tagline: King of soundstage, amazing vocal timbre, superb mic
tws-samsung-galaxy-buds4-pro.review: The vocal timbre is great. Very clean, wide and clear. Front-to-back depth and top-to-bottom staging are much better than the Buds 3 Pro. The planar timbre is much better than the 3's. Still the king of transparency mode. ANC is better than the 3's. Downside: replacement eartips are still hard to find.

tws-huawei-freebuds-pro-5.tagline: Superb mic; iOS/Android/Windows ready, no ecosystem lock-in
tws-huawei-freebuds-pro-5.review: Samsung won't open multipoint to iOS or non-Samsung Android; here nothing is locked. The app is on iOS, Android and even macOS. Sound is broadly like the Buds4 Pro but with more around 500 Hz; very mid-forward overall (watch his YouTube review). EQs fine. Technicalities are great too, but for natural timbre Samsung and Sony are still the champions in my view. The planar timbre here is still a little less natural, but far better than the metallic, pointy FreeBuds Pro 4.

tws-samsung-galaxy-buds-3-pro.tagline: King of soundstage, king of transparency, superb mic
tws-samsung-galaxy-buds-3-pro.review: Best price for every feature you need! Open-sounding soundstage that's outside your head, amazing, open-back style. 1 DD + 1 planar. U-shaped, a bit bright. King of transparency: super clear, like you're not wearing TWS at all. ANC comfort isn't Sony level yet but it's fine. The mic is ridiculously clear. Downsides: the slide volume control is a bit fiddly, and the codec is nerfed (supposedly only good with Samsung's SSC), but honestly AAC on my phone was fine too. The drivers are just nice. Ultra-HQ codecs aren't that important if the driver is good. Other downside: the eartips are squarish and hard to find. (Full review on his YouTube.)

tws-sennheiser-momentum-true-wireless-5.tagline: Replaceable battery, best mic among bean-shaped TWS
tws-sennheiser-momentum-true-wireless-5.review: You can replace the TWS battery yourself. Not a big improvement over the 4, just a better fit. ANC is up and the mic is waaay better, even better than Sony's; among bean-shaped TWS this is probably the best right now. Same tonality, same soundstage.

tws-devialet-gemini-ii.review: FANTASTIC IMMERSIVE IMAGING. Great depth: front-to-back is wonderful, not just left-right. Spacious, wide. It's like having an acoustically treated room with a good sub and Atmos bars. ANC is as quiet as Sony and Bose. A really fun tuning, and the bass is very mature. I haven't heard a TWS with imaging like this. Has EQ too. Fun sounding, but the price is too high.

tws-soundcore-liberty-5-pro-max.review: The best noise reduction in the industry; the AI noise reduction is excellent. Sound is still U-shaped: very bassy, very high highs. Better than before, though: the treble can be tamed, the bass not yet. Timbre and staging aren't much better than the Liberty 4. ANC is excellent, clean, no suction feeling; by Soundcore standards it now rivals Sony's LinkBuds. Fit is very comfy.

tws-earfun-air-pro-4.review: Fantastic quality for the price. Good timbre. Soundstage and imaging are spacious. The September 2026 firmware adds PARAMETRIC EQ. Sub-bass slam rumbles deeper than the regular 4 and can rival the H3. Wide separation. ANC is quiet and its noise response keeps getting better. Battery lasts forever. (Full review and comparison on his YouTube.)

tws-airpods-pro-3.tagline: God-tier mic on iOS, superb ANC
tws-airpods-pro-3.review: Very good mic; voice isolation only works with iOS devices. Still no custom EQ. Sounds bright around 4–10 kHz, lots of sub-bass. Loudness-dependent EQ: the lower the volume, the bassier and brighter; the higher the volume, the less treble and sub. Still no multipoint with non-Apple devices. (Full review on his YouTube.)

tws-bose-quietcomfort-earbuds.review: I underestimated it at first because the QC Ultra was too V-shaped, even with EQ. This one's default tuning has good timbre and feels grand. The bass is deep, and surprisingly there's a nice vocal emphasis too. Not as bright as the Accentum either. Out of the box, no EQ, it sounds super good and will satisfy non-hobbyists and hobbyists alike. Downside: no aptX, so very sensitive listeners may want a bit more treble clarity. The ANC has NO RIVAL, sorry: at 2 million rupiah its ANC can beat even the XM5. The mic is a bit weak in crowded places. (Full review on his YouTube.)

tws-sony-wf-1000xm5.review: One of the most advanced ANCs: naturally quiet, with lots of customisation. Two chips and three feedback mics with a great wind cover that pick out and suppress sound very well. Sounds better than the XM4 with the new Driver X: more clarity, cleaner vocals, a wider soundstage and vibrating bass rumble. Better mic than the XM4 as well. (TWS battle review on his YouTube.)

tws-sony-linkbuds-fit.review: The lightest, most comfortable Sony. Compared with Bose and the Accentum, this fit is by far the nicest. ANC is good but lets a little treble through. Same driver as the XM5, and the same ANC technology, just a different fit and tips, so the tuning differs slightly, but resolution, clarity and staging are equally very good. Better mic than the XM5, and its noise reduction doesn't keep switching on and off. So many features it makes your head spin.

tws-sennheiser-accentum-tws.review: It sounds in the same direction as the Sennheiser Momentum 4, with a slightly better mic. The only real difference is punch: it doesn't thump as hard as the Momentum. That's the main thing. Imaging and soundstage are nearly the same; separation and detail differ only a tiny bit, with a better fit. Just buy this. Very affordable. Good ANC too, about LinkBuds S level. 2-YEAR WARRANTY.

tws-huawei-freebuds-pro-4.review: Sound quality is more or less the same as the 3. The timbre is better: the mids aren't buried as much. But the treble is still a bit bright; you can still hear ringing and sizzle. It's OK. EQ still doesn't work unless Android's Absolute Volume is turned on. I'm sure the mic is fine judging from YouTubers' reviews; I couldn't test it, I only tried it at a mall. ANC isn't much different: highs still get through, not Sony or Bose level. But the 3 will surely be discontinued, so like it or not, this is where you go.

tws-huawei-freebuds-pro-3.review: U-shaped. VERY GOOD IMAGING: height, depth, width. Airy and very open sounding. ANC is very decent and quiet, though I think the LinkBuds and Bose QCE are still better. Immersive, with a wide-open soundstage and imaging; clean, a bit bright. Less punchy than Sennheiser, but the imaging and soundstage are spacious if you like a slightly U-shaped tuning. Well priced too. The timbre is a bit unnatural.

tws-edifier-neobuds-pro-2.review: It destroys the value of overpriced TWS like Jabra, JBL and Marshall. A Knowles balanced armature + single DD with an active crossover. Crunchy, aggressive mids. A really good microphone. The most advanced parametric EQ. Deep ANC. 4 mics on each bud for calls. Downsides: a bit sharp at the top of the treble, 10 kHz and up; the mids are a bit recessed. Edifier needs to make its custom EQ even better.

tws-tozo-aerosound-6-pro.tagline: Budget semi-parametric EQ, king under 1 million rupiah
tws-tozo-aerosound-6-pro.review: It nails tonal correction really well; you can get it to JM-1. Treble-rich. Long battery. SEMI-PARAMETRIC EQ, which Soundcore and EarFun can't do yet. With a super good MIC too for this price. TOZO is on fire! (Video review on his YouTube.)

tws-soundpeats-h3.review: Wow, this is the bean-shaped version of the EarFun Air Pro 4. Wide, good separation, good imaging, and best of all the sub-bass extension is deep and really fun, but not basshead either. Loses on battery, and the timbre is plasticky compared to the Air Pro 4. He covers everything in his video.

tws-earfun-air-pro-4-2.review: Hard to beat. aptX Lossless, 52-hour battery, good mic, OK ANC, Auracast, under a million rupiah. On features alone it's hard to beat. Sound is fine too: the treble is safer than the Air 2 and Air 3, which have a bit too much and are a little spicy. The Free Pro 3 is slightly warmer with nice timbre and a touch wider imaging, but overall I prefer this tuning; its mids are better. The FP3 loses on ANC, mic, battery, codec and features. If you want it all, nothing under a million beats this. Round eartips, not square or keyed like Huawei's and the L4NC's. (Full review on his YouTube.)

tws-bose-quietcomfort-ultra-2nd-gen.review: KING OF ANC. Too quiet, too silent, like diving into water. If you love noise cancelling, this is the answer. Sound is just OK; I even prefer the QCE. Still very V-shaped, same as gen 1. The mic is much improved. Fit is nice though it looks a bit big. Only the price is pretty steep. Choose this if you like lots of bass, a good mic, and ANC with no rival. (Full review on his YouTube.)

tws-samsung-buds-3-fe.review: It's OK, in the same direction as the Buds 3 Pro. The mic is a bit below it and the treble is warmer; the technicalities just aren't at the Pro's level. The rest is just "fair". If you want amazing sound go for the 4+ or H3, but this won't be bad. It's enough, with an OK mic.

tws-sony-wf-c710n.review: The tonality is a bit warm up top and a bit thick in the bass, so it comes across warm and bassy, missing a little upper mids or lower treble. It can be EQ'd; I made an EQ for it. Imaging is also nicer than the C700. For sound I still like the Air Pro 4: wider, bigger and cleaner. But this isn't bad either, if you like the bean shape. Good mic. ANC is okay, not XM5 level, but for the price it's fine; the isolation helps. Transparency is nice, though there's a little white noise when it's quiet. (Video review on his YouTube.)

tws-edifier-neodots.review: Just so-so. V-shaped and a bit bright, still like the NeoBuds Pro 2. Better with EQ: the Classic/Classical preset (I forget which) is already an improvement. Codec is still only LDAC, no aptX Lossless in 2024. Mic is OK. But there's no multipoint like the NeoBuds Pro 2. Battery is very strong, but the official site doesn't say how long it lasts with ANC on.

tws-earfun-air-pro-4i.review: At around 500 thousand rupiah there's no denying it: it has no rival. Worth every penny. Separation and imaging are a little below the Air Pro 4 (different driver). Features are above the Air 2 since it has ANC too, and the game mode is the same as the Air Pro 4. The tuning is a bit bright at 4–8 kHz, but that can be fixed and brought in line with the Space Travel 2. (Full review on his YouTube.)

tws-moondrop-pudding.review: It wins if you like the bean shape. I think the Space Travel 2 is right on value and price, but its case doesn't close; this one's does. Boomy in the sub-bass, bright around 8–11 kHz, but it has an 8-band parametric EQ. Mic is not bad, better than the 4i. Separation and soundstage are better than the 4i / 4 Pro / Aerosound 6. ANC is better than the 4i, 4 Pro and Aerosound 6.

tws-earfun-free-pro-3.review: Bean-shaped, for sports. Good driver, nice EQ, pleasant. Very detailed for a single-DD TWS: the driver has fairly fast transients, so lots of detail comes through clearly. The treble is still a bit forward for me, so I cut it. Sounds better than the L4NC. I still think the 4i is better, but if you want the bean shape, don't hesitate. Think about what you need. (Full review on his YouTube: TWS from 100k to 1 million rupiah.)

tws-huawei-freebuds-6i.review: Not stingy with codecs like Samsung, where you must use a Samsung phone: this has LDAC on any phone. Against the EarFun FP3 it only loses on imaging; tuning is in the same class. Wins on mic and ANC. It has a low-latency mode too, though I don't know how low. U-shaped tuning, in the direction of the FreeBuds Pro 3. Great mic. ANC is quieter than the L4NC; use cozy/general mode, as ultra has hiss. The up/down volume slider is really nice. Only loses on battery to the L4NC. A bit bright. Loses to the Air Pro 4 and 4i overall. (Full review on his YouTube: TWS from 100k to 1 million rupiah.)

tws-soundcore-liberty-4nc.review: LDAC, multipoint, 50-hour battery, 3 AI mics, custom EQ. The sound isn't sharp and piercing any more like the regular Liberty 4. Adaptive ANC, super deep and silent, and adjustable. Superb transparency with dual vocal/ambient modes. The sound still leans bassy, but the treble doesn't pierce any more. (Full review on his YouTube: TWS from 100k to 1 million rupiah.)

tws-sony-linkbuds-s.review: Classic Sony: the bass, the space. The texture, depth and width are a bit different from Sennheiser, and so is the resolution. I prefer the CX Plus. Both are warm, but this one's technicalities are drier: you still don't quite get the reverb tails and midrange detail. The WF-C500 sounds on par with this, or even better. (TWS battle review on his YouTube.)

tws-sony-wf-1000xm4.review: It has LDAC and the best ANC technology, with auto ANC and a custom EQ. Basically great: as a Sony fanboy this is a must-have. Its LDAC is the most stable, not buggy, and not as battery-hungry as the NeoBuds and Liberty 3 Pro.

tws-redmi-buds-6-pro.review: Good ANC, good mic, a warm, slightly muddy, vocal-centric tuning with sweet vocals. Downsides: separation is a bit blurry, and the piezo and dynamic drivers aren't quite coherent. I'd still pick the Air Pro 4 for the sound; the mic is slightly better here. (Full review on his YouTube.)

tws-tozo-golden-x1.review: Bright, too bright: I can't cut the air treble. The Aerosound 6 Pro's treble is much safer. Skip it; same price anyway.

tws-edifier-w260nc.review: Right for a consumer with a budget who doesn't want a lot of fuss: wants the AirPods stem look but cheap, no logo on the body, and good. Good mic, proper ANC. The sound is just balanced and safe. Mic is better than the Free Pro 3, fit is fine. Tuning and technicalities: the Free Pro 3 is nicer once EQ'd. Not basshead like the P40i or Liberty 4 NC either. ANC is quieter than the L4NC.

tws-moondrop-space-travel-2.tagline: Best tuning under 500k; skip the Ultra
tws-moondrop-space-travel-2.review: Good tuning, neutral-leaning and mid/vocal-centric; not much sub-bass. Separation and imaging are a little better than the Air 2, and this has better timbre, tuning and mids. Good mic, has ANC and transparency: OK, not amazing. Louder volume. The custom parametric EQ is nice. DON'T BOTHER WITH THE ULTRA: bright at 4–5 kHz with sibilance, expensive, weird planar timbre, adds no stage or imaging, also bright at 8 kHz. I tried EQing it and couldn't get it as natural and organic as the non-Ultra. (Full review on his YouTube.)

tws-soundcore-liberty-5.review: A very bassy tuning. Only the ANC improved over the 4 NC; the rest is more or less the same, and I prefer the 4 NC's tonality. If you still have a 4 NC, keep it. (Full review on his YouTube.)

tws-earfun-air-2.review: Sounds in the same class as the Engine 4; I slightly prefer the Engine 4's treble, but this one's mids and lows are good. Neither will disappoint for the sound. The mic is much better here, though: 4 noise-cancelling mics. Gaming mode at 55 ms, multipoint. But like the Engine 4, no ANC. Stem-shaped. (Full review on his YouTube: TWS from 100k to 1 million rupiah.)

tws-soundpeats-engine-4.review: Sounds good, and EQs really well. Timbre and stage are good compared with the SoundPeats Mini or even the Capsule 3 Pro. Its weakness is no ANC, that's all; if something's lacking, just boost it. The mids are clean and pretty. Its strength is the sound. Already beaten by the EarFun 4i. (Full review on his YouTube: TWS from 100k to 1 million rupiah.)

tws-soundcore-p40i.review: The NEW BEST TWS from Soundcore. The sweet spot, priced under the L4NC; the upgrade from the Dot 3i! Better mic, superb ANC + transparency. The sound leans V-shaped but can be EQ'd, and the upper mids are nice and transparent; good driver, 11 mm like the L4NC. Has a gaming mode too. (Full review on his YouTube: TWS from 100k to 1 million rupiah.)

tws-soundcore-liberty-3-pro.review: Sounds good, very bassy though. Wide soundstage. But the fit is too big. My advice now: get the EarFun Free Pro 3 instead. This one's discontinued.

tws-nothing-cmf-buds-pro.review: At launch, around 700k rupiah, it wasn't great, but now it's 500k, so it can be an alternative to the legendary Dot 3i. ANC is noticeable, and there's EQ, though as soon as you switch EQ on the sound changes and gets a bit messy; I prefer to stay on Balanced. Worth it at 500k; at 700k skip it. No multipoint yet.

tws-soundcore-life-dot3i.review: THE BENCHMARK at around 500k rupiah. Has EQ and ANC, and it's good and responsive. Physical buttons, not touch; comfortable. Mic is decent. Battery is fine. The cheap version of the Liberty 3 Pro if you can't afford that yet. Don't buy the Note 3i: its upper mids are aggressive and not smooth enough. Just buy the Dot 3i.

tws-nothing-ear-2.review: White, transparent, AirPods-style: Apple kids who hang out at coffee shops in loose Uniqlo basics with a MacBook will surely love it. If you've already decided to buy it for the design, just buy it; whatever I say, you'll buy it anyway. From me: the driver is good, the tuning is lacking. You can EQ it, but there's a fatal flaw: the moment EQ is on, the whole volume drops and it's not loud enough. ANC is OK and quiet but still not as natural as the C700 or LinkBuds S. Come on, you're already sure; you just wanted my audio-book's validation, right? Here, I've added it.

tws-nothing-ear-2024.review: More or less the same as the Ear 2. The tuning is ordinary, but people love it for its indie transparent look and want affirmation of the sound. Nothing's driver isn't bad (DMS says the same), but as a gadget its options are very lacking in my personal opinion. The EQ is a mess: switch EQ on, still flat, and suddenly the sound changes, gets patchy and weird, and the volume drops. If you like the default tuning, go for it. Mic is not bad. There, you've got your affirmation.

tws-soundcore-space-a40.review: Get the P40i instead; its tuning will be friendlier to TWS lovers' ears. This one sounds neutral, not bassy: good for people who like neutral and balanced. EQs fine. 50-hour battery. Has LDAC. Only 1 MILLION rupiah.
